Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a weekly payment of up to £123.25, paid by your employer for up to 28 weeks if you are unable to work due to illness.  You can receive the full amount of SSP or 80% of your normal weekly earnings, whichever is lower, and it is calculated based on your average weekly earnings over an 8-week period.  SSP is paid by your employer in the same way as your regular wages and is subject to tax and National Insurance deductions.  To qualify for SSP, you must be an employee who has worked for your employer and been ill for at least one full working day.

This document outlines the compensation and expenses related to jury service in England and Wales.  While jury service itself is unpaid, individuals can claim reimbursement for lost earnings, travel expenses, and childcare costs.  Employees can claim specific amounts for travel, food, and childcare, while self-employed individuals and those not working can claim for travel expenses only.  Employers are obligated to provide time off for jury service, but can request delays if necessary.  Individuals can also seek compensation for lost earnings from the court if their employer does not pay them during service.

Universal Credit is replacing Housing Benefit and income-related ESA, and you may need to switch if your circumstances change or you receive a "Migration Notice."  You will continue receiving other benefits you currently receive, such as PIP or Carer's Allowance, but certain benefits may be reduced when you claim Universal Credit.  Eligibility for Universal Credit includes being on a low income, being out of work or working, or unable to work due to a health condition.  You must meet specific criteria, including living in the UK, being 18 or over, and having less than £16,000 in assets.

This document outlines the requirements for filing a tax return in the UK, focusing on individuals who are self-employed, partners in businesses, or have specific financial situations.  It highlights that tax returns are necessary if certain income thresholds are met, including self-employment income exceeding £1,000, capital gains tax payments, and specific income types like rental income or foreign income.  The document also emphasizes the importance of registering for Self Assessment by October 5th if you need to file a tax return, and provides guidance on claiming tax reliefs and paying voluntary National Insurance contributions.  Finally, it encourages individuals to register for Self Assessment to ensure compliance with tax obligations.

The MOT test ensures road safety and environmental compliance for vehicles.  Vehicles must undergo an MOT by a specific anniversary date, with exceptions for vehicles needing testing at one year old.  If the MOT expires, vehicles cannot be driven or parked on public roads, but can be driven to a repair shop or pre-arranged MOT test.  The MOT certificate provides information on the expiry date, and reminders can be set up to avoid fines.  Driving without a valid MOT can result in fines up to £1,000.
